plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Tall shrubs in the wild, crowned with fiery bracts that look like petals. The true flowers are the tiny yellow-green clusters at the center. In its native range, whole hillsides glow scarlet as the year closes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (roughly November through February)
plants.location: Southern Mexico, including the hills of Guerrero and Oaxaca, its native range
plants.funFact: The colorful parts are modified leaves called bracts. They change color in response to the long nights of late autumn. The Aztecs called the plant cuetlaxochitl and used it to make dye.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: A tropical cactus with arching, segmented stems. It drips with bright, asymmetrical flowers in late autumn and winter. In gardens and homes across the Northern Hemisphere it brings color to the darkest weeks of the year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November through January in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil, and widely grown indoors in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: This cactus grows on trees in Brazilian forests rather than in deserts. Long nights and cool temperatures trigger its buds.

plants.name: Callistemon citrinus
plants.description: An Australian shrub whose flower spikes look like bright red bottle brushes. The spikes are made of long, showy stamens and are covered in nectar. They draw honeyeaters and lorikeets, which feed noisily in the branches in the warm southern summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring through summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with a strong flush from October to January
plants.location: Eastern Australia, including New South Wales and Queensland, where it grows along streams and in gardens
plants.funFact: The woody seed capsules can stay on the branch for years. They often release their seeds only after a fire or when the branch dies.
